name: Cheque and Deposit Fraud
description: Counterfeit, altered or stolen cheques, and deposits of items later returned, can be used to obtain funds before the fraud is discovered. Mule accounts and overpayment scams are common.

sources.text: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (specify year, e.g. 2025)
Industry guidance on funds availability and check clearing (general)

indicators.name: Large cheque deposited followed by prompt withdrawals
indicators.canon: Large credit followed by prompt withdrawals
indicators.desc: A cheque deposit or refund is credited and quickly withdrawn or transferred before it clears or is verified.
indicators.ctx: Funds are drawn before the cheque clears.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Cheque appears altered or counterfeit
indicators.desc: Image shows alterations, mismatched MICR or font.
indicators.ctx: Image shows alterations, mismatched MICR or font.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Deposit of third-party cheque from unknown payer
indicators.canon: Payments from or to unrelated third parties
indicators.desc: Funds are paid or received, or instructions are given to pay, through parties with no evident link to the customer, contract, debt or insured interest. Includes third-party cheques, loan repayments, premiums, gaming funds and goods payments not matching the documentation.
indicators.ctx: Payee and depositor have no relationship.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Overpayment request after receiving cheque
indicators.canon: Overpayment by cheque or money order from an unknown party
indicators.desc: A cheque or money order from an unknown party exceeds the amount due and a refund of the excess is requested before clearance.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: seller is asked to refund an overpayment before the cheque clears.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)
